historical_record.description: Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 50, Golden Gate Park Conservatory, by Ordinance No. 314-72.

Put up in 1878–79 by the greenhouse makers Lord & Burnham of Irvington, New York, who had fabricated it for James Lick; after Lick died in 1876 with the crates unopened, twenty-seven San Franciscans bought it from his estate and gave it to the park. Modeled on the conservatory at Kew, with 33 tons of glass on a wood and iron frame.
Partly destroyed by fire in 1883 and rebuilt the next year, helped by a $10,000 gift from Charles Crocker.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1972; also a California Historical Landmark.
The City Planning Commission approved the proposal to designate the Golden Gate Park Conservatory as a Landmark, on the 2 August 1972 recommendation of the Landmarks Preservation Advisory Board.

In its capital improvement review the City Planning Commission unanimously raised the Golden Gate Park Conservatory rehabilitation project (No. 651.74.103) from a B to an A priority and found it in conformity with the Master Plan; $40,000 had already been contributed from private sources toward the matching funds.
